block: Phase B builder B1: SW Line Items leaf rows in cost centres APPLB2B, APPLCCO, APPLSUPPLYOPS, APPLSUPFPO, APPLTDDIST, APPLFIFINANCE, INTEGM, APPLLUBRICANTS, APPLAETOTAL, APOLLO

rules.note: Columns A and B carry the mapping values present in the source file on all 291 lines of this centre, reading Commercial Fuels and Supply, with no line blank and no second value. Column D names the centre Chief Commercial Officer. The destination is read straight from the source file, so it is not derived. These 291 lines include 14 Snowflake recharge lines and 1 data tool charge line that the source file keeps with this centre, while the same products sitting in the pooled corporate centre APPLH_INFOTECH go to Enterprise Data / Data, and per person Adobe licence lines that it keeps here rather than sending to a workplace tooling destination. That is the adjudicated convention applied across this block: the cost centre in column C decides, everywhere except the pooled corporate centre APPLH_INFOTECH, which lies outside this block.

Columns A and B carry the mapping values present in the source file on all 106 lines of this centre, reading Commercial Fuels and Supply. Column D names the centre SUPPLY OPERATIONS, which matches the Supply platform held by the structure inside the Commercial Fuels portfolio.

Columns A and B carry the mapping values present in the source file on all 229 lines of this centre, reading Commercial Fuels and Supply. Column D names the centre FUEL PRICING & OPTIMISATION. 213 of the 229 lines name Salesforce in column N and the source file still keeps those lines with the centre, which is one of the proofs of the adjudicated convention that a product name does not move a line off its cost centre.

Columns A and B carry the mapping values present in the source file on all 33 lines of this centre, reading Commercial Fuels and Trading & Shipping. This is the one centre in the block whose mapping value is Trading & Shipping rather than Supply, which is why it is a rule of its own rather than folded into the Commercial Fuels centres above.

Columns A and B carry the mapping values present in the source file on all 125 lines of this centre, reading B2B & Energy Solutions and B2B. The structure states that no Lubricants platform exists and that one must not be invented; the source file settles the destination as the B2B platform, so nothing is invented here.

rules.match: Column C (cost centre) = APPLB2B, taking the lines whose column N (document text) is outside the AmpolFM licence allocation text captured by rule 10
rules.note: Column D names the centre B2B, and the structure holds a B2B platform inside the B2B & Energy Solutions portfolio, so the centre name in column D and the platform value are the same word. The mapping values present in the source file put cost centre APPLLUBRICANTS on that same portfolio and platform (rule 5), which shows the B2B platform is the destination the source file uses for the commercial B2B centres in this workbook. The centre content is consistent with the reading: card processing maintenance and its Oracle support with the matching monthly amortisations, the enterprise sales system renewals with the matching amortisations, distributor systems (Companion licences, transponder costs, diesel truckstop support), marketplace management fees, application support retainers, electronic signature renewals, card reporting recharges and the per person Adobe, Copilot and Salesforce recharges. The twelve AmpolFM licence lines are separated into rule 10 so the transfer stays visible; the destination is the same, so no dollar moves between the two rules.

Restated to the whole centre. Column D names the centre AMPOL ENERGY TOTAL, and 752 lines at 2,903,834.95 is the leaf total of that centre to the cent. Column N names the destination in the source file's own words across the largest blocks in the centre: Energy Solutions Azure recharge on twelve monthly lines, move any expenditure for IT Energy Solutions on twelve more, reallocate ES from AmpEnergy to ES, and Snowflake Energy Solutions recharges. The rest is the same estate: energy retail billing invoices, EnergyEdge subscriptions, electric vehicle charging platforms and charge point data feeds, an energy monitoring subscription, and the customer platform licence blocks with the monthly amortisations that follow the licence block. The structure holds Energy Solutions as a platform inside the B2B & Energy Solutions portfolio. S8574, the Foregenix PO7000250967 payment card industry certification chargeback of 14,935.20 and the only line in the centre on cost element 801425, is inside this rule under the adjudicated convention that the cost centre decides; naming a security product does not by itself place a line on Cyber.

Column D names the centre PROJECT APOLLO, a significant item centre. Twenty six of the forty lines, 1,233,117.87 of the 1,234,782.87, are transfers into this centre whose column N ends in a move to SI, and each has its source line in cost centre APPLAETOTAL at the equal and opposite amount under the adjacent CO document number. Ten of those transfers carry a stated identifier on both sides: the purchase order PO7000244846 links S18675 to S8664, S18681 to S8714, S18698 to S8879 and S18702 to S8929, and the invoice references INV04573 and INV04790 link S18703, S18705 and S18707 and S18704, S18706 and S18708 to the matching APPLAETOTAL lines. The transferred content is Ampol Energy spend: mass market billing licences, the billing migration purchase order, retail electricity operating expenditure and the Apollo software licence. The structure states that significant item programs land on real project platforms and it holds no Apollo platform, so the destination is the platform the transferred spend comes from, which rule 7 fixes as Energy Solutions. The remaining fourteen lines, 1,665.00, are per person Adobe licences and a contact centre payment with its clearing and variance entries, booked to the same centre.

Contra form. Each of the twelve CO documents carries one charge leg of 15,000.00 in cost centre APPLB2B and one contra leg of -15,000.00 in cost centre APPLMTOTAL, both on cost element 801482 and both reading the same column N text, "FMG AMPOLFM LICENCE 2025_ALLOC TO F&I" on the first six documents and "FMG AMPOLFM LICENCE 2026_ALLOC TO F&I" on the last six. The charge legs are S6056, S6076, S6494, S6776, S6990, S7211, S7429, S7654, S7664, S7884, S8310 and S8567; the contra legs are S11896, S11905, S11952, S12071, S12098, S12141, S12171, S12211, S12920, S12949, S12987 and S13101, in document order. Each document also carries the two parent rows that duplicate these children, APPLBULKFUEL above APPLB2B and APPLMARKETING above APPLMTOTAL, which are not leaf rows and are not counted. Each leg follows its own centre: the APPLB2B charge leg lands on B2B & Energy Solutions / B2B with the rest of that centre under rule 6, and the APPLMTOTAL contra leg sits outside this block, where phaseb_b3 rule 13 places it on Ampol Retail / Store Operations and lists the same twelve documents in its contra_documents record. The transfer therefore stays visible on both sides. The words ALLOC TO F&I in column N are not a destination the ledger acts on: the document moves the licence out of the marketing operating centre and into APPLB2B, and column C is where it lands.
